outline.chapter_title: Introduction to the Challenges of Scaling Large Language Models
outline.description: Sets the stage by describing the rapid growth of LLMs, their performance benefits, and the associated computational, memory, and environmental costs that motivate low‑bit research.
subtopics: Historical growth of LLM size and capability
Compute, memory, and energy bottlenecks in modern LLMs
Motivation for model compression and quantization
Overview of post‑training quantization vs. training‑time low‑bit methods

outline.description: Covers the theoretical background of quantization, including uniform vs. non‑uniform schemes, stochastic rounding, and why 1‑bit and ternary representations are attractive for matrix multiplication.
subtopics: Quantization basics: bits, dynamic range, and precision
Uniform quantization and clipping
Ternary ({-1,0,1}) and binary (+/-1) weight representations
Impact of quantization on arithmetic operations (add vs. multiply)
Energy models for different arithmetic precisions

outline.chapter_title: The BitNet Architecture: From FP16 Transformers to BitLinear
outline.description: Introduces the original BitNet design, explaining how a standard Transformer is transformed by replacing linear layers with BitLinear and the resulting computational paradigm.
subtopics: Review of the standard Transformer block (nn.Linear, RMSNorm, etc.)
Design goals of BitNet: eliminating multiplications
Structure of BitLinear: integer addition based matrix multiplication
Integration with other components (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings)
Compatibility with open‑source ecosystems (HuggingFace, vLLM, llama.cpp)

outline.chapter_title: BitNet b1.58: Design Details and Quantization Functions
outline.description: Delves into the specific modifications that produce the 1.58‑bit (ternary) variant, focusing on the weight and activation quantizers and their implementation tricks.
subtopics: Why add a zero state? From 1‑bit to 1.58‑bit representation
AbsMean quantization function for weights – derivation and intuition
RoundClip operation and stability considerations
γ scaling factor – computation and role in training stability
Activation quantization: symmetric range [-Qb,Qb] vs. zero‑point scaling
Training pipeline: from scratch training with 8‑bit activations

outline.description: Presents practical guidelines for reproducing BitNet b1.58 models at various scales, including data preprocessing, token budgets, optimizer choices, and hyper‑parameter schedules.
subtopics: Dataset selection – RedPajama token count (100B) and preprocessing steps
"2T token" experiment – scaling token budget and its effect
Optimizer settings (AdamW vs. others) adapted for ternary weights
Learning rate schedules and warm‑up strategies for low‑bit training
Regularization techniques compatible with ternary weights (weight decay, dropout)
Implementation tips: mixed‑precision (FP16 activations) and hardware kernels
